title: pvVisItMiliReader
body:
## pvVisItMiliReader

Reads Mili, LLNL's engineering results database used by structural finite-element codes: open the .mili JSON root file, from which the plugin locates the per-processor state files. The output is a multiblock of unstructured meshes with materials and node and element results over time. ParaView 5.13.3 has no native Mili reader; the Mili plugin is an optional part of the VisIt bridge. One file supplies every time step the format stores.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The VisIt bridge builds the Mili plugin only when ParaView is compiled with the Mili library; other ParaView builds lack this reader.
- Name the arrays you need in PointArrays and CellArrays (materials in Materials): the VisIt bridge starts with every variable unselected, so omitting them normally gives geometry without fields.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue and has not run a native acceptance check for this reader; check meshes, arrays and times on your own data.

Native constructor: `VisItMiliReader`. Identity: `sources/VisItMiliReader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CellArrays` | Names of the zone-centred (cell) variables to read from Mili data; each becomes a cell-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The Mili plugin offers node and element results stored in the Mili database; which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FileName` | Path of the single Mili file to read (.m, .mili); the reader takes every time step the format stores from it. Use an absolute path; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). Name the .mili JSON root file; it locates the state files. Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"minLength":1,"type":"string"}` | `required` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `Materials` | Names of materials to convert into volume-fraction cell arrays. For each selected material the bridge adds a float cell array named after it: 1 in cells made only of that material, its volume fraction in mixed cells and -1 where it is absent. The Mili plugin offers the materials defined in the Mili database. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `Meshes` | Names of the Mili meshes to read. Each selected mesh becomes one named block of the multiblock output and unlisted meshes are skipped. The Mili plugin reports one unstructured mesh per Mili mesh; take the names from the reader's available list. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `PointArrays` | Names of the node-centred (point) variables to read from Mili data; each becomes a point-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The Mili plugin offers node and element results stored in the Mili database; which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvVisItMiliReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
  }
}
```
